questions.question: Explain oral communication. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain oral
  • communication.
  • Oral communication is the exchange of information through spoken words.
  • It includes conversations, meetings, presentations, speeches, and telephone
  • calls. It allows immediate feedback and clarification, making it an effective
  • method of communication. Features include quick interaction, personal
  • contact, and emotional expression. Effective oral communication requires
  • clear speech, confidence, proper tone, and active listening.

questions.question: Explain formal letters. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain formal letters. Formal letters are official written communications used in business or
  • professional contexts. They follow a standard format including sender’s
  • address, date, receiver’s address, subject, salutation, body, closing, and
  • signature. They are used for purposes such as job applications, complaints,
  • enquiries, and official requests. Formal letters maintain a polite tone, clarity,
  • and professionalism.

questions.question: Analyze importance of mass communication. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze importance
  • of mass
  • communication.
  • Mass communication refers to the process of transmitting information to a
  • large audience through media such as television, radio, newspapers, and
  • the internet. It plays a crucial role in spreading information, education, and
  • entertainment to society. Mass communication helps in shaping public
  • opinion, promoting awareness about social issues, and supporting
  • democratic processes. It also assists businesses in advertising and
  • marketing their products. In modern society, mass communication connects
  • people globally and supports cultural exchange and knowledge
  • dissemination.

questions.question: Discuss the role of rhythm in effective speech. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of
  • rhythm in effective
  • speech.
  • Rhythm in speech refers to the pattern of stressed and unstressed sounds
  • that create flow and clarity in speaking. A good rhythm helps maintain
  • audience interest and improves the effectiveness of communication. It
  • involves proper pacing, pauses, emphasis, and variation in tone. Rhythm
  • makes speech more engaging, easier to understand, and memorable.
  • Effective speakers use rhythm to highlight key points and maintain audience
  • attention.
